A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SignBind-LLM, and their main text, equations, figures and tables are readable. However, v3 includes supplementary Sections A–F, while v4 ends after its references despite repeatedly referring to supplementary material. Comparison of those later supplementary details is therefore limited.

before.justification: V3 reports original translation and fingerspelling results on How2Sign, BOBSL and ChicagoFSWild+, with ablations, linguistic analyses and qualitative examples in the main text and supplement.

after.justification: V4 reports original benchmark results, decoder-scale comparisons, component and fusion ablations, and a fingerspelling confusion matrix.

M1.justification: Sections 3.3–3.5 change fusion inputs from expert logits to penultimate embeddings, explicitly discarding the expert CTC heads. Manual–lip sigmoid mixing is replaced by manual-query/lip-key-value cross-attention; cross-attention was previously an alternative ablation. The default decoder also changes from LLaMA-2-7B to Flan-T5-XL.

E1.justification: Both versions use YouTube-ASL for pre-training and evaluate How2Sign, ChicagoFSWild+ and BOBSL, covering ASL/BSL translation and fingerspelling. Zero-shot YouTube-ASL-to-How2Sign transfer and How2Sign-only training already appear in v3 Appendix B.2.

E2.justification: The main How2Sign and BOBSL comparator sets are retained. V4 Table 3 omits Pannattee et al. and Gajurel et al., reported at 48.0% and 48.4% in v3. V4 Table 7 also omits several YouTube-ASL comparison configurations from v3 Table 9, including its joint-training block.

E3.justification: The decoder study changes from 1B/3B/7B Llama models to 250M/780M/3B Flan-T5 models, introducing a decoder-size-matched comparison with prior methods. The reported fusion transformer changes from six layers in v3 Appendix D.3.2 to four in v4 Section 4.3. V4 additionally reports fingerspelling precision and recall.

E4.justification: V4 adds a fingerspelling confusion matrix and revises the fusion comparison to test gating plus cross-attention. Component removal, stand-alone experts, decoder variation, temporal offsets and transfer analyses already existed in v3. V4 retains selected POS findings, but its referenced full supplementary analysis is unavailable.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. Results remain point estimates; the added confusion matrix and precision/recall do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Reported best results change from 22.1 to 23.1 How2Sign BLEU-4, 6.8 to 7.0 BOBSL BLEU-4, and 73.2% to 73.6% fingerspelling accuracy. Component, temporal-alignment and stand-alone results also change, and new decoder-scale, routing-accuracy and precision/recall results appear. These are revised results under changed architecture/decoder settings, not established same-setting improvements.

T1.justification: The fusion definitions are substantively revised: v3 Equations 10–12 project logits and apply sigmoid mixing, whereas v4 Equations 8–12 project embeddings and define multi-head cross-attention with residual/FFN processing. This changes the mathematical formulation, but adds no theorem or proof.

C1.justification: V4 adds prominent claims that performance advantages persist at matched 250M decoder scale and that training requires 259 GPU-hours, approximately 124 times less than SSVP-SLT. These architectural-attribution and comparative-efficiency claims become central in the abstract, introduction and conclusion; the three-stream design and state-of-the-art claims remain.

C2.justification: V3 Appendix B.1 favors lightweight gating because cross-attention offers negligible benefit at greater complexity. V4 instead emphasizes cross-attention as the mechanism resolving variable temporal offsets. It also explicitly limits the lipreading stream to mouthings rather than grammatical mouth gestures and adds occlusion/resolution/motion-blur explanations for letter confusions. Semantic-drift failures were already documented in v3.

D1.justification: V4 adds routing-label construction, temperature annealing details, the BOBSL realignment source and a planned code/data/model release, while revising compute reporting. The supplied v4 lacks v3 Appendix D’s detailed prompts, phonemization fallback, optimizer/LoRA tables and inference settings. This substantially changes available reproducibility documentation, although retention in the referenced but unavailable supplement cannot be established.

R1.justification: V4 adds references supporting Flan-T5, improved BOBSL alignment and the linguistic rationale for fusion, while dropping several background and omitted-baseline references. The central positioning around jointly modeling signing, fingerspelling and lipreading remains. Related-work compression is primarily a structural revision.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work and method explanations are extensively rewritten. Related work contracts from four subsections to two, ablations become a separate main section, and selected supplementary analyses are integrated into the main narrative.

P2.justification: V4 adopts a single-column layout and redraws both overview diagrams. Table 1 gains decoder, parameter and compute columns; fusion/pre-training tables are consolidated; selected v3 supplementary examples are reformatted into Table 4; and a new confusion-matrix figure appears. These are substantial display changes beyond renumbering or numerical updates.

improvement.justification: Matched-decoder comparisons and clearer fusion documentation strengthen v4. However, its unavailable supplement prevents checking the retention of detailed reproducibility and limitation evidence. New inconsistencies also weaken reliability: Table 7 gives gated fusion 22.3 BLEU-4 while the prose says 23.1, and Table 3 implies a 2.5-point fingerspelling advantage despite the claimed 2.1 points. These benefits and unresolved problems prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
